Package CSE222HW2

Class Inventory

  • java.lang.Object
    • CSE222HW2.Inventory
  • public class Inventory
extends java.lang.Object
    Represents an inventory management system for electronic devices.

    The Inventory class manages a collection of electronic devices and provides functionality for adding, removing, updating, displaying, and exporting the inventory.

    It uses a LinkedList to store ArrayLists of the 5 device categories.

    • Method Detail

      • add

        public void add()
        Adds a new device to the inventory.

        The user is prompted to enter the category, name, price, and quantity of the device. If the user inputs a category name other than "Smartphone", "Smart Phone", "Tablet", "Headset", "TV" or "Laptop", the method will throw an exception and quit the program. If the user inputs a name that already exists, the method gives a warning and returns to the main menu. The device is then added to the appropriate category list.

        The add method of the ArrayList has a time complexity of O(n) since it resizes dynamically everytime we call the add method. Time complexity will be O(n) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, therefore the time complexity will be O(5n) which will give us O(n). The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).

      • remove

        public void remove()
        Removes a device from the inventory.

        The user is prompted to enter the name of the device to remove. If the device exists, it is removed from the inventory.

        The remove method of the ArrayList has a time complexity of O(n) since it goes through the entire List to find the object to remove. Time complexity will be O(n^2) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, when it finds the device to be removed it will call the remove method which has a time complexity of O(n), therefore the time complexity will be O(5n^2) which will give us O(n^2). The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).

      • update

        public void update()
        Updates the details of a device in the inventory.

        The user is prompted to enter the name of the device to update, then they can choose to update the price and/or quantity of the device.

        Time complexity will be O(n) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, therefore the time complexity will be O(5n) which will give us O(n). The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).

      • display

        public void display()
        Displays the list of devices in the inventory.

        This method prints details of all devices in the inventory, including category, name, price, and quantity.

        Time complexity will be O(n) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, therefore the time complexity will be O(5n) which will give us O(n). The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).

      • minimumPrice

        public void minimumPrice()
        Finds and displays the device with the minimum price in the inventory.

        This method iterates through all devices in the inventory and finds the one with the minimum price. It then prints the details of that device.

        Time complexity will be O(n) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, therefore the time complexity will be O(5n) which will give us O(n). The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).

      • sortwithPrice

        public void sortwithPrice()
        Sorts the devices in the inventory by price and displays the sorted list.

        This method creates a new ArrayList of devices sorted by their prices in ascending order. It then prints the details of devices in the sorted list.

        The add method of the ArrayList has a time complexity of O(n) since it resizes dynamically everytime we call the add method. Time complexity will be O(n^2) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, all of the devices will be added to a new ArrayList to sort with price, the add method has a time complexity of O(n), therefore the time complexity will be O(5n^2) which will give us O(n^2).

      • totalvalue

        public double totalvalue()
        Calculates and returns the total price value of the inventory.

The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).

      • restock

        public void restock()
        Restocks or reduces stock for a device in the inventory.

        This method allows the user to restock or reduce the stock quantity of a device in the inventory. The user is prompted to enter the name of the device and choose whether to add or remove stock. Then they can specify the quantity to add or remove.

        Time complexity will be O(n) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, therefore the time complexity will be O(5n) which will give us O(n). The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).

      • exportInventory

        public void exportInventory()
        Exports the inventory details to a text file.

        This method writes the details of all devices in the inventory to a text file, including the category, name, price, and quantity. Additionally, it calculates and writes the total number of devices and the total inventory value to the file.

        Time complexity will be O(n) if we say the device number in the ArrayList is n since there is a nested loop, the first for statement will iterate five times since there are only five categories, therefore the time complexity will be O(5n) which will give us O(n). The rest are all simple statements and have a time complexity of O(1).
